member.name: T:Victoria.Enums.ExceptionSeverity
member.summary: severity of the exception

member.name: F:Victoria.Enums.ExceptionSeverity.COMMON
member.summary: Cause is known and expected, indicates that there is nothing wrong with the library itself

member.name: F:Victoria.Enums.ExceptionSeverity.SUSPICIOUS
member.summary: Cause might not be exactly known, but is possibly caused by outside factors. For example when an outside service responds in a format that we do not expect

member.name: F:Victoria.Enums.ExceptionSeverity.FATAL
member.summary: If the probable cause is an issue with the library or when there is no way to tell what the cause might be. This is the default level and other levels are used in cases where the thrower has more in-depth knowledge about the error

member.name: T:Victoria.Enums.TrackEndReason
member.summary: Specifies the reason for why the track ended.

member.name: F:Victoria.Enums.TrackEndReason.Finished
member.summary: This means that the track itself emitted a terminator. This is usually caused by the track reaching the end, however it will also be used when it ends due to an exception.

member.name: F:Victoria.Enums.TrackEndReason.Load_Failed
member.summary: This means that the track failed to start, throwing an exception before providing any audio.

member.name: F:Victoria.Enums.TrackEndReason.Stopped
member.summary: The track was stopped due to the player being stopped by either calling or .

member.name: F:Victoria.Enums.TrackEndReason.Replaced
member.summary: The track stopped playing because a new track started playing. Note that with this reason, the old track will still play until either its buffer runs out or audio from the new track is available.

member.name: F:Victoria.Enums.TrackEndReason.Cleanup
member.summary: The track was stopped because the cleanup threshold for the audio player was reached. This triggers when the amount of time passed since the last call to AudioPlayer#provide() has reached the threshold specified in player manager configuration. This may also indicate either a leaked audio player which was discarded, but not stopped.

member.name: T:Victoria.Rest.Filters.ChannelMixFilter
member.summary: Mixes both channels (left and right), with a configurable factor on how much each channel affects the other. With the defaults, both channels are kept independent from each other. Setting all factors to 0.5 means both channels get the same audio.

member.name: T:Victoria.Rest.Filters.DistortionFilter
member.summary: Distortion effect. It can generate some pretty unique audio effects.

member.name: T:Victoria.Rest.Filters.EqualizerBand
member.summary: Equalizer band

member.name: P:Victoria.Rest.Filters.EqualizerBand.Band
member.summary: 15 bands (0-14) that can be changed.

member.name: P:Victoria.Rest.Filters.EqualizerBand.Gain
member.summary: Gain is the multiplier for the given band. The default value is 0. Valid values range from -0.25 to 1.0, where -0.25 means the given band is completely muted, and 0.25 means it is doubled.

member.name: T:Victoria.Rest.Filters.KarokeFilter
member.summary: Uses equalization to eliminate part of a band, usually targeting vocals.

member.name: T:Victoria.Rest.Filters.LowPassFilter
member.summary: Higher frequencies get suppressed, while lower frequencies pass through this filter, thus the name low pass.

member.name: T:Victoria.Rest.Filters.RotationFilter
member.summary: Rotates the sound around the stereo channels/user headphones aka Audio Panning. It can produce an effect similar to: https://youtu.be/QB9EB8mTKcc (without the reverb)

member.name: P:Victoria.Rest.Filters.RotationFilter.Hertz
member.summary: The frequency of the audio rotating around the listener in Hz. 0.2 is similar to the example video above.

member.name: T:Victoria.Rest.Filters.TimescaleFilter
member.summary: Changes the speed, pitch, and rate. All default to 1.

member.name: T:Victoria.Rest.Filters.TremoloFilter
member.summary: Uses amplification to create a shuddering effect, where the volume quickly oscillates.

member.name: T:Victoria.Rest.Filters.VibratoFilter
member.summary: Similar to tremolo. While tremolo oscillates the volume, vibrato oscillates the pitch.
